model_annotation: Figure 4, located in the top portion of the page, illustrates the performance of various knowledge editing methods on long-tail biomedical knowledge, as evaluated on the CiKT dataset. The plot displays the performance of five methods—Base, MEMIT, FT, IKE, and ROME—across different co-occurrence number groups, which are categorized as <10¹, [10¹, 10²), [10², 10³), and ≥10³. The x-axis represents these co-occurrence groups, labeled with their respective ranges, and uses a categorical scale with tick marks for each group. The y-axis represents performance in percentage (%), ranging from 55% to 65%, with tick marks at 55, 60, and 65, and is scaled linearly. Each method is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker: Base (black with circle markers), MEMIT (green with square markers), FT (blue with triangle markers), IKE (red with diamond markers), and ROME (purple with star markers). All lines are solid. The Base line remains relatively flat across all groups, starting at approximately 58.5% and ending at about 58.0%. The MEMIT line shows a slight upward trend, beginning at around 59.0% and rising to approximately 63.5%. The FT line starts at about 58.0% and increases to roughly 59.5%. The IKE line begins at approximately 58.0% and rises to about 61.0%. The ROME line starts at around 58.5% and increases to approximately 63.0%. The plot visually indicates that performance generally improves as the co-occurrence number increases, with MEMIT and ROME showing the most significant gains.
